title: Exact-conductor translation-forced Hayes zeros
statement: Let j>=1. Among binary Hayes characters of exact level j, translation fixes one character for j=1, no characters for even j, and 2^((j-1)/2) characters for odd j>=3. At odd polynomial degree, the number of these fixed characters with negative translation sign, hence with zero Mangoldt and squared-discrepancy Fourier coefficient, is one for j=1, zero for even j, and 2^((j-3)/2) for odd j>=3. At even polynomial degree the forced-zero count is zero at every level.

evidence.supports: Exact character, translation-fixed, and negative-sign counts at every admitted conductor level, together with recovery of the cumulative totals.
evidence.notes: The universal proof is the difference of the cumulative fixed-dual and negative-sign counts under restriction. Exhaustion through level eight is a mutation control, not quantifier evidence.

provenance.source: exact conductor filtration of the Hayes translation-fixed dual

notes: For odd j>=3 the forced-zero fraction is 2^(-(j+1)/2), not 2^(-(j-1)/2). The theorem does not supply WITT-LOW or REL credit.
